endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: CM.AW-P2: Mechanisms for obtaining feedback from individuals (e.g., surveys or focus groups) about data processing and associated privacy risks are established and in place.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether gathering patient feedback on AI data processing and privacy preferences changes design decisions or brings AI data practices closer to patient expectations. The recommendation currently rests on a single framework endorsement from the CHAI Assurance Standards Guide.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Without comparative or even descriptive data, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The endorsement reflects expert consensus, which GRADE treats as distinct from evidence of effect.

The one endorsing source, the CHAI Responsible AI Guide, lists feedback mechanisms such as surveys or focus groups as a practice that should be established (CM.AW-P2). This is a voluntary framework expectation and is not a binding regulatory requirement among the sources supplied here.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare AI products developed with and without structured patient privacy feedback, measuring whether feedback alters data handling choices, patient-reported trust, or privacy complaints. Descriptive work documenting how often AI data practices diverge from stated patient privacy expectations would also establish the size of the hazard.
commentary.underserved_note: No test of this practice was supplied, so no evidence includes Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Feedback methods such as surveys and focus groups may underrepresent these groups unless they are offered in multiple languages and accessible formats, and that possibility remains untested.
